kpis.name: S&P 500
kpis.note: Broad equity risk-on/risk-off signal. High VIX or S&P drawdown signals demand risk for Southwire construction end markets.

kpis.name: Brent Crude
kpis.note: Energy costs affect Southwire manufacturing and logistics. Sustained Brent >$90 pressures freight and resin input costs.

kpis.name: Copper (LME)
kpis.note: Primary raw material. Copper content of wire drives COGS. Sustained elevation compresses margin unless hedged or repriced.

kpis.name: Aluminum (LME)
kpis.note: Key input for aluminum wire and cable. Price signals secondary cost pressure and hedge calendar triggers.

kpis.name: Freight (Drewry WCI)
kpis.note: Ocean freight index drives import costs on raw materials and packaging. WCI >$4K signals elevated supply chain risk.
kpis.change: Monitor Drewry WCI weekly for rate momentum

kpis.name: VIX
kpis.note: Equity market fear gauge. VIX >25 indicates risk-off environment; monitor customer demand signals and receivables.

kpis.name: Natural Gas
kpis.note: Energy input for manufacturing and logistics. Sustained elevation pressures margin. Drives residential heating demand indirectly.

kpis.name: Gold
kpis.note: Risk sentiment indicator. Gold >$3,000 with VIX elevation signals macro uncertainty that may dampen CapEx spending by customers.

wire.title: Suicide is up among Black Americans. We need to talk about it.
wire.summary: NPR's Michel Martin hosted a panel conversation about mental health and suicide in the Black community, exploring a difficult subject in deeply personal conversations.

wire.title: New U.S. indictment charges former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro with torture
wire.summary: U.S. authorities added new torture charges to their case against former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, ramping up pressure on the ousted authoritarian leader already fighting drug trafficking allegations.

wire.title: 4 people on NASA's Crew-12 mission return to Earth after 8 months in space
wire.summary: Four people — two NASA astronauts, one from the European Space Agency and a Russian cosmonaut — spent nearly eight months at the space station, conducting spacewalks, science experiments and research.

wire.title: White House correspondent April Ryan reflects on reporting while under attack
wire.summary: Ryan has spent decades pressing presidents for answers. She talks about access, power, race and how asking questions put her in President Trump's crosshairs. Her new book is Notes on a Blacklash .

wire.title: South Korea to recall its ambassador to Ukraine over North Korean POW dispute
wire.summary: The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

wire.title: South Korea test-flies its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon
wire.summary: The test follows North Korea's recent hypersonic missile test. Tensions between the Koreas have increased after land mine explosions injured three South Korean soldiers near the border. North Korea denies responsibility.

wire.title: Isaias intensifies to hurricane. And, judge orders Pike execution evidence preserved
wire.summary: People in the Gulf are preparing for bad weather this weekend after Isaias intensified into a hurricane. And, a judge has ordered Christa Pike's failed execution evidence be preserved.

wire.title: Strike on Ukrainian public bus leaves 30 dead as blackouts worsen in Kyiv
wire.summary: Russian strikes in eastern Ukraine have killed 30 people and injured at least 18, according to authorities. The attacks included a strike on a public bus and have worsened power outages in Kyiv.

wire.title: ICE has quietly used this warehouse as a detention facility all summer, neighbors say
wire.summary: Throughout the summer, rumors have been bubbling in North New Jersey that ICE has quietly been using a warehouse as a detention center. NPR investigated.

wire.title: Medical debt is crushing hospital patients in LA. Health officials may have a fix
wire.summary: In Los Angeles County, the nation's most populous, a new system could screen hospital patients for financial aid, preventing hundreds of thousands from getting bills they can't pay.

wire.title: Russian strike on buses kills at least 30, say officials, as deadly attacks on Ukraine surge
wire.summary: Ukraine accused Russia of targeting two crowded vehicles in the front line city of Kramatorsk to kill as many civilians as possible.

wire.title: Christa Pike now walking after failed US execution, lawyer tells BBC
wire.summary: A lawyer says the murderer of Colleen Slemmer is moving around her hospital room after surviving two lethal injections.

wire.title: Venezuela's ex-leader Nicolás Maduro charged with conspiracy to commit torture
wire.summary: The new accusations relate to the alleged torture of US citizens held in Venezuela while Maduro was in power.

wire.title: Residents airlifted to safety after flooding in central Chile
wire.summary: The Mapocho river has burst its banks after an unusually large amount of rain fell in recent days.

wire.title: Italy approves elections overhaul as opposition accuse Meloni of 'scam'
wire.summary: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni says the move will deliver more stable government, but opposition parties say her aim is to stay in power.

wire.title: US deportations to African countries unlawful and exploit suffering, rights group says
wire.summary: More than 500 migrants have been expelled from the US to African countries, HRW says, citing US data.
